comparison: Both support protein diffusion measurements (C1-C4, C180). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment while peer reviewers accepted these as convincing control data showing normal diffusion behavior. High agreement (Jaccard 0.833).

Both support fluorescein diffusion measurements (C5-C12). OpenEval notes concern about 24hr time-dependent changes while peer reviewers accepted the extensive dataset without specific critique. Partial overlap (Jaccard 0.533) as peer R2 also covers C19-C25.

Both support CCF2 measurements (C13-C18). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of pKa determination and diffusion measurements, while peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of the overall charge-dependent diffusion pattern. Perfect match (Jaccard 1.0).

Both support acidic molecule measurements (C19-C25). OpenEval evaluates pKa determination and diffusion data, while peer reviewers accepted these as baseline comparisons for basic drugs. Partial overlap (Jaccard 0.467) as peer R2 also covers C5-C12.

Both support dramatic reduction in basic drug diffusion (C30-C44, C177-C178). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of concentration independence and BSA controls, while peer reviewers endorsed this as a central finding. Strong overlap (Jaccard 0.714).

OpenEval R5 includes background on Doxorubicin aggregation in buffer (C26-C29), which peer R13 accepted without challenge. Minor overlap (Jaccard 0.211) as these claims contextualize the in-cell measurements.

Both support Quinacrine time-dependent diffusion changes (C45-C59). OpenEval emphasizes progressive sequestration concerns, while peer reviewers accepted these measurements as part of the extensive dataset. Perfect match (Jaccard 1.0).

Both support findings on compounds with low fractional recovery (C60-C65). OpenEval notes methodological limitations while peer reviewers accepted these as consistent with the overall pattern. Perfect match (Jaccard 1.0).

Both support background literature on lysosomal sequestration mechanisms (C66-C73). OpenEval validates citations while peer reviewers accepted this established knowledge. Partial overlap (Jaccard 0.242) as peer R14 covers broader background.

Both support Bafilomycin experiments showing slow diffusion persists despite reduced lysosomal sequestration (C74-C85). OpenEval calls this critical and somewhat speculative, while peer reviewers endorsed the mechanistic approach. Strong overlap (Jaccard 0.6).

Both support sodium azide experiments (C86-C90). OpenEval notes speculative interpretation while peer reviewers accepted the mechanistic findings. Partial overlap (Jaccard 0.25) as peer R6 primarily focuses on Bafilomycin data.

Both strongly support the Doxorubicin/N-acetyl-Doxorubicin comparison (C91-C97). OpenEval calls this elegant, peer reviewers praised it as 'inciteful' with demonstrated relevance to drug development. Strong agreement (Jaccard 0.7).

Both strongly support N-acetylation improvements in fractional recovery (C98-C102, C117-C118). OpenEval notes well-designed strategy, peer reviewers endorsed relevance to drug development. Perfect match (Jaccard 1.0).

Both support negative results from organelle staining experiments (C103-C106). OpenEval notes importance of reporting limitations, peer reviewers accepted comprehensive mechanistic approach. Perfect match (Jaccard 1.0).

Both support summary findings comparing buffer vs. cell diffusion (C107-C113). OpenEval emphasizes cell extract limitations, peer reviewers endorsed implications for drug design. Strong overlap (Jaccard 0.636).

Both support mechanistic conclusion that protonatable groups cause slow diffusion (C114-C116, C128, C136-C137). OpenEval identifies this as central insight, peer reviewers strongly endorsed the pKa modification experiments. Partial overlap (Jaccard 0.231).
OpenEval R15 includes lysosomal inhibitor experiments (C114-C115, C136), which peer R6 accepted as part of mechanistic findings. Minor overlap (Jaccard 0.13).
Both support pKa correlation with diffusion (C119-C120, C179). OpenEval notes limited compound number and non-linearity, peer reviewers accepted this as key finding. Perfect match (Jaccard 1.0).

Both support implications for drug-target interactions and design (C121-C127). OpenEval notes these are logical inferences rather than tested hypotheses, peer reviewers endorsed relevance to drug optimization. Strong overlap (Jaccard 0.556).
OpenEval R17 includes critique of drug design practices (C125, C127), which peer R10 endorsed as pointing to important issues. Minor overlap (Jaccard 0.125).

OpenEval rates claims about increased activity from N-acetylation (C129-C130, C138) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of activity assays, while peer reviewers SUPPORTED these as reasonable implications for drug development. Disagreement on level of evidence required. Partial overlap (Jaccard 0.25).
Both support background literature on drug properties and cellular complexity (C131-C159). OpenEval validates citations, peer reviewers accepted contextual framing. Strong overlap (Jaccard 0.735).

OpenEval SUPPORTS Line-FRAP methodology (C160-C166) with appropriate citations, while peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN due to significant concerns about statistical presentation, error bars (SEM vs. SD), and data display. Disagreement on methodological rigor. Perfect claim overlap (Jaccard 1.0) but different evaluation types.

Both support compound identity and validation that measurements reflect molecular diffusion (C167-C176). OpenEval emphasizes critical controls, peer reviewers accepted compound selection as relevant. Perfect match (Jaccard 1.0).

Both support summary claim of 10-20 fold slower diffusion in cells vs. buffer (C177-C178). OpenEval validates quantitative range, peer reviewers accepted as central finding. Minor overlap (Jaccard 0.118) as peer R3 covers broader Doxorubicin data.
